record_body:
Account summary
- Prospect came inbound after reading the public benchmark report (latency/$) and asked for a live walkthrough + “what exactly did you do to get those numbers?”
- Primary driver: build an internal legal assistant (EU clients) with strict confidentiality. They’re currently prototyping on a hosted provider but expect to move to VPC once they reach production.
- Strong interest in Redwood Private (VPC) and/or Dedicated capacity in EU region(s) to hit consistent p95 latency.

Use case / workload notes (from calls + emails)
- Workload mix:
  - Document retrieval (embeddings) + answer synthesis (chat completion)
  - Long-context summarization of legal memos/contracts (4k–32k context range mentioned)
  - Occasional reranking for retrieval relevance
- Non-functional:
  - “p95 matters more than average” (their app is user-facing and used in live client calls)
  - Cost sensitivity is meaningful but secondary to compliance + predictability (they need to forecast spend for enterprise contracts)
  - Wants clear levers: batching, caching, quantization profiles, fallback/routing controls

Benchmark methodology questions (verbatim-ish)
- “Is caching enabled in the benchmark? If yes, what kind and how do you prevent it from flattering results?”
- “What was the concurrency and prompt distribution? Our workload is very prefill-heavy with long docs.”
- “How many runs did you do per region and how stable were the p95s?”
- “Can we reproduce the methodology for a shortlist of models in eu-west?”
- They asked for:
  - Methodology details: warmup, token mix, concurrency levels, rerun/variance gates, exclusion criteria
  - The exact disclaimer language we use when comparing across regions/providers

Security / compliance requirements captured
- Must-have items for vendor onboarding:
  - SOC 2 Type II report (and ideally ISO27001 statement)
  - SSO/SAML for Console access + role-based access controls
  - Audit logs and admin event tracking (who changed model routing/policies)
  - Data retention controls for logs (ability to set or minimize retention; separate policy for prompt/response logging)
  - EU data residency: process/store in EU only for production traffic; clear statement around support access
  - KMS integration options for encryption keys in Private (customer-managed preferred)
- Data handling questions:
  - Explicitly asked whether prompts/responses are used for training (they require “no training by default” and strong contractual language)
  - Redaction: they want confirmation that public benchmark artifacts do not leak operational details (IDs/tokens)

Activity timeline
- 2025-06-28: Account created (inbound form from benchmark landing page; interest marked: Private/VPC + EU latency)
- 2025-07-02: Benchmark walkthrough call w/ Lukas Meyer + Markus Klein; prospect brought security lead + product lead. Shared methodology overview; agreed to follow up with written answers + security package. (See Fireflies link.)
- 2025-07-03: Markus sent “reproducibility notes” email + offered a technical session with Applied ML to map their workload (prefill-heavy) to our published workload mixes.
- 2025-07-08: Summit requested formal security review kickoff + vendor questionnaire turnaround in <10 business days.
- 2025-07-15: Summit confirmed internal champion (Director of Product) but flagged security as gating item; asked for EU region coverage statement and log retention defaults.

Internal notes / sales guidance
- Positioning angle that resonated:
  - “Production economics with transparent methodology + stability gates; not just peak tokens/sec.”
  - “Same interface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; start with Hosted PoC, then move into VPC for production.”
- Messaging caution:
  - Do not claim universal ‘fastest’ results; keep to ‘in our tests / under defined workloads’ + point to methodology + caveats.

Proposed plan (next 2–3 weeks)
1) Security package: provide SOC2 (under NDA if required), security overview for Redwood Private (VPC), logging/retention defaults, and data residency language for EU deployments.
2) Methodology deep dive (45 min): bring Jonas Weber or Claire Dubois for the ‘how we measured’ section; tailor to prefill-heavy long-context + p95 variance handling.
3) Scoped PoC: 2 models, 1–2 EU regions; success criteria: p95 < their target and cost per 1M tokens within budget; include fallback policy + audit logging demo.

Open questions to resolve
- Which EU region(s) are acceptable for residency and latency? (They asked for confirmation of ‘EU-only’ routing.)
- Do they require customer-managed keys day 1 or is Redwood-managed acceptable short-term?
- What is their real production concurrency? They gave ranges but no hard numbers.

Contacts (as captured)
- Champion: Director of Product (name not yet confirmed in CRM)
- Stakeholders: Security lead + Solutions architect

Health
- Medium-positive. Strong urgency + clear need for VPC, but security requirements are strict and timeline depends on document turnaround.
